    Altria Yields 5.9%. Here's How Many Shares You'd Need for $5,000 in Yearly Dividend Income.

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (454 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Lawrence Rothman, CFA – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:14PM EST.
    • It has been revealed that altria Group (MO +0.25%) has a remarkable dividend history.
    • In a recent development, the firm has prioritized dividends, and management targets mid-single-digit percentage increases annually.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Lawrence Rothman, CFA – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:14PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Altria Group ›.

    It has been revealed that altria Group (MO +0.25%) has a remarkable dividend history. It has raised the payment 61 times over the last 57 years. That puts the manufacturer firmly among the Dividend Kings — a small group of stocks with active payout-hiking streaks of at least 50 consecutive years.

    In a recent development, the firm has prioritized dividends, and management targets mid-single-digit percentage increases annually. It met that target this year by raising the quarterly payout by 4.7% to $1.11 per share.

    That annualizes to a payout of $4.44 a year, which at Friday's closing share price of $74.87 gives it a dividend yield of 5.9%. For comparison, the S&P 500 index yields 1.1%.

    In a recent development, what if you're targeting a specific amount in annual dividends — say, $5,000? To get that, you'd need to purchase 1,126 shares for about $84,300. Of course, that assumes Altria Group's dividends will remain constant, which they haven't, obviously.

    But before income investors make a decision about purchasing this high-yielding Dividend King, they should take a deeper look at Altria Group's underlying business fundamentals.

    The maker of tobacco and e-vapor products has been watching its product sales volumes decrease for some time. That's particularly true for its core cigarette business, which falls under its smokeable tobacco group.

    In the first nine months of this year, smokeable tobacco products' revenue, excluding excise taxes, increased 3.6% year over year. However, this increase came entirely from the company increasing the prices it charges. The volume of cigarettes and other smokeables it sold dropped 2.7%, primarily driven by cigarettes' 2.8% volume decline.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, relying on a regular cadence of price increases on smokers to offset volume declines isn't a recipe for long-term success. While Altria management remains committed to paying and raising its dividends, it can't fight weakening business fundamentals forever. While the dividend seems secure for now, the manufacturer's relatively high 89% payout ratio suggests that may not be the case forever, unless the business finds other ways to raise its revenues.

    That's why I think investors looking for dividends can find better alternatives.

    #119512. Tech Report: Ray Dalio says Bessent move is sign that a debt crisis is getting closer; recommends gold and bitcoin

    📅 21 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (625 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Ray Dalio says Bessent move is sign that a debt crisis is getting closer; recommends gold and bitcoin

    📅 21 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.
    • Industry observers note that the Bridgewater Associates founder mentioned Bessent's initiative to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S.
    • Recent findings suggest that "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

    Industry observers note that the Bridgewater Associates founder mentioned Bessent's initiative to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

    Recent findings suggest that "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Industry observers note that dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

    According to recent reports, the U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio remarked. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

    Recent findings suggest that bessent remarked in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

    Industry observers note that after years of overspending, Dalio said total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

    Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

    To solve this, Dalio stated the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

    Recent findings suggest that first, Dalio noted the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the Fresh York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

    "All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio mentioned. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic.".

    Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he said.

    Recent findings suggest that dalio stated it's vital to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

    Dalio noted the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed.".

    To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

    As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder said.

    It has been revealed that dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.

    10 stocks we like better than BridgeBio Pharma ›.

    Recent findings suggest that on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 29, 2026, BridgeBio (BBIO -2.75%) announced net product revenue of $253.2 million for Attruby, up 134% year over year. Commercial momentum across rare disease therapies expands the tech giant's addressable market beyond $8 billion in peak annual sales.

    Three things management mentioned stand out.

    It has been revealed that growth for Attruby, a treatment for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (a heart condition caused by misfolded proteins), stems from newly introduced patients starting therapy first rather than switching. Comparative real-world data showing reduced hospitalizations reinforce management's long-term sales projections.

    The manufacturer expects a Food and Drug Administration decision by its Nov. 27, 2026, target action date under the Prescription Drug User Fee Act for BBP-418, a potential treatment for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I (a genetic muscle disease). Management has identified over 500 patients in the U.S.

    According to recent reports, priority reviews by regulatory authorities set early target action dates for infigratinib in achondroplasia (a genetic bone growth disorder) and encaleret in autosomal dominant hypocalcemia type 1 (a rare hormone disorder). These approvals would expand the organization's commercial rare disease portfolio in 2027.

    Three commercial releases arrive within seven months, marking an operational shift. Management relies on field teams and digital tools to broaden prescriber coverage while expanding margins toward corporate breakeven.

    A balance sheet holding $1.5 billion supports these launches while funding late-stage clinical development.

    #119508. 3 AI Hardware Stocks Down More Than 30% From Their Records to Buy Now and Hold Through 2030

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (889 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    3 AI Hardware Stocks Down More Than 30% From Their Records to Buy Now and Hold Through 2030

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (889 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that nvidia (NVDA -14.01%), Coherent (COHR -12.90%) and Dell Technologies (DELL -11.04%) all supply the same artificial intelligence (AI) build-out.
    • Nvidia closed at a record $239.24 on Oct.
    • But their businesses haven't followed the stocks down.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:43PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Industry observers note that nvidia (NVDA -14.01%), Coherent (COHR -12.90%) and Dell Technologies (DELL -11.04%) all supply the same artificial intelligence (AI) build-out. Nvidia makes the chips, Coherent makes optical parts that carry data between them, and Dell builds the servers they go into.

    All three stocks have also tumbled. Nvidia closed at a record $239.24 on Oct. 6 and trades around $153 as I write this, about 36% lower. Coherent, near $223, is off about 48% from its June 2 record close. And Dell, roughly $322, is about 45% under the $588.40 record close it set on Sept. 17.

    But their businesses haven't followed the stocks down. Each firm's latest report shows data center demand still growing, and I think each stock now leaves room for gains through 2030.

    In a recent development, on Nov. 11, Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO and made Colette Kress, the chief financial officer, interim CEO while it looks for a permanent one.

    Industry observers note that the business, though, kept speeding up. In the fiscal third quarter of 2027, which ended Oct. 25, 2026, Nvidia's data center revenue hit $107.6 billion. It was 21% above the previous quarter, and sequential growth accelerated from 18% in fiscal Q2. Management expects around $130 billion in total revenue for the fiscal fourth quarter, but that period has an extra week.

    Shares still dropped about 3% the day after the Nov. 17 report. Using analysts' average forecast for fiscal 2028 (the year ending January 2028), the stock costs under 10 times earnings, while the forward price-to-earnings ratio of the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) is around 18.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    The CEO search might keep some investors wary for a while. But for a business whose data center sales more than doubled year over year, I think the stock is cheap.

    Coherent's lasers and optical transceivers move data between chips inside a data center, and between data centers.

    Recent findings suggest that showing how much AI now powers the company, Coherent's datacenter and communications segment took in $1.95 billion in its fiscal first quarter of 2027 (which ended Sept. 30, 2026), or 82% of total revenue. Segment sales rose 79% year over year and 21% sequentially, up from $1.09 billion a year before and $1.62 billion in fiscal Q4 2026.

    For a 2030 holder, the longer deals might matter more. Coherent signed one for its fresh PhotonLink optics platform worth around $20 billion over five years, with revenue starting to ramp in early 2028. Also, on Nov. 18 the board approved a share buyback program of up to $2 billion, around 5% of Coherent's market value at the current stock price.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Granted, operating cash flow was negative $93 million last quarter, and Coherent spent another $776 million on fresh equipment and facilities to expand capacity. And at around 22 times earnings using analysts' fiscal 2027 forecasts (that year ends in June 2027), it's the priciest of the three. Still, with management expecting pro forma revenue growth (which leaves out businesses it sold) over 60% this fiscal year, I'd call that valuation reasonable.

    It has been revealed that dell's AI server orders are arriving faster than Dell is shipping them. In its fiscal second quarter of 2027 (which ended July 31, 2026), the organization booked a record $60.9 billion in AI server orders, almost four times the $16.4 billion in AI server revenue it recorded. It closed the period with a record $95 billion AI server backlog.

    Total revenue rose 58% year over year to $47.0 billion. And with management guiding to non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share of $25.50 this fiscal year, the stock trades at around 13 times those earnings.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    But profits have outpaced cash. Dell's operating cash flow dropped 13% year over year to $2.2 billion in fiscal Q2, even as net income more than tripled to $4.1 billion. A significant reason is financing receivables (money customers owe Dell under financing deals), which cut operating cash flow by around $6.7 billion in the quarter. The fiscal third-quarter report on Tuesday, Nov. 24, might show whether more of that cash is starting to come in.

    All three stocks might continue to slide together if AI spending cools. But each tech giant is growing fast, and I think each trades at a valuation that leaves room for that growth to reach shareholders by 2030.

    I'd start with Nvidia, the cheapest of the three relative to its expected earnings and the one whose data center growth accelerated last quarter. Coherent would be next, with its multiyear PhotonLink deal. Dell is worth a look too, but I'd keep the position smaller until its cash flow catches up to its profits.

    Latest Update: The 'debasement trade' returns after Bessent bond maneuver. Crypto and gold are back in style

    📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (864 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The debasement trade is gaining new traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.
    • The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S.
    • "The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," remarked Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The debasement trade is gaining new traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

    The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

    "The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," remarked Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

    It has been revealed that gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

    Bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

    Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

    According to recent reports, the U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

    Recent findings suggest that the Treasury Department stated last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the plans.

    Recent findings suggest that last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "big toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

    Industry observers note that long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

    According to recent reports, "Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold noted in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

    The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

    The stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah remarked. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

    The Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah mentioned. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

    "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah said in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

    Industry observers note that coltman at 21Shares said the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

    Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

    It has been revealed that deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh mentioned in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

    Billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder said.

    Industry observers note that "The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

    It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, remarked Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

    Industry News: Should You Buy Tesla or SpaceX Stock Before Their Potential Merger?

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (823 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.
    • While it's long been rumored that Elon Musk could move to combine Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) and Tesla (TSLA -7.64%), the megamerger is closer to a reality than it's ever been.
    • Industry observers note that the upcoming company would combine SpaceX's artificial intelligence capabilities and infrastructure with Tesla's physical AI (self-driving cars and robots), potentially benefiting from vertical integration and scale.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Levy – Nov 22, 2026 at 5:01PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.

    While it's long been rumored that Elon Musk could move to combine Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) and Tesla (TSLA -7.64%), the megamerger is closer to a reality than it's ever been. The two companies are in advanced discussions, and a merger announcement could come as soon as next month, according to Bloomberg.

    Industry observers note that the upcoming company would combine SpaceX's artificial intelligence capabilities and infrastructure with Tesla's physical AI (self-driving cars and robots), potentially benefiting from vertical integration and scale. Investors considering an investment in either Tesla or SpaceX ahead of any merger announcement need to consider what they stand to gain from a deal and what they're giving up.

    It has been revealed that A merger of Tesla would be an all-stock deal with SpaceX paying Tesla shareholders in stock to absorb the tech giant. That dilutes existing SpaceX shareholders' stock, but they end up owning a piece of a larger company.

    Tesla shareholders could benefit in the short term. Acquisitions usually require the acquiring tech giant to pay a premium for the acquired company’s shareholders to agree to sell their shares. But that premium can swiftly disappear in an all-stock deal. If the market thinks the acquiring company overpaid, it can send the share price lower well ahead of the merger closing, decreasing the actual value received.

    According to recent reports, furthermore, Tesla's share price will become pegged to SpaceX's performance until the deal closes. Anyone considering owning Tesla stock needs to be comfortable with the idea that SpaceX’s financials will impact its share price.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    That's a key question, given that SpaceX stock is at the moment priced for significant revenue growth over the next few years. It holds major contracts with multiple AI companies to sell infrastructure at a premium price and plans to add a whopping 10 gigawatts of capacity in 2027, building on the 1.7 gigawatts it ended the third quarter with. Achieving that expansion and selling its full capacity while maintaining its high pricing would result in phenomenal growth, but that two-step process is far from guaranteed.

    At the same time, investors need to be comfortable with the fact that even if SpaceX and Tesla agree to a merger, it might not receive approval. SpaceX is a contractor with the U.S. government. Tesla's ties to China -- its Shanghai plant built more than half its vehicles in 2025 -- could deter regulators from approving the deal.

    Industry observers note that that said, other U.S. defense contractors have been able to maintain operations in China, maintaining a firewall between different segments. However, that could limit the potential synergies between SpaceX and Tesla.

    Finally, SpaceX buyers have to be comfortable with acquiring Tesla. The majority of the auto manufacturer's value is based on the potential of its fledgling robotaxi business and its humanoid robotics. Neither generates any meaningful revenue at this point, and Musk has been prone to overpromising and underdelivering on Tesla's real-world AI implementations.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that while a merger has potential benefits and drawbacks for regular Tesla and SpaceX shareholders, Musk would be the clear winner. Any merger agreement will likely ensure Musk maintains majority control over the vote at the combined company. That means Tesla shareholders have to be comfortable with Musk having the freedom to practically do whatever he wants with the business.

    Sources indicate that to be sure, both Tesla and SpaceX investors are already likely major fans of Musk. He has full control over SpaceX, and Tesla shareholders eventually approved a $1 trillion pay package for Musk last year, as he threatened to leave the company if voters didn't pass it. Musk previously posted on X that he wants at least 25% voting control at Tesla, "enough to be influential, but not so much that I can't be overturned." If the merger goes through, however, he will have enough control to avoid being overturned.

    Sources indicate that this might not be a significant problem to most shareholders, but it's certainly something to consider. There are many public companies where the CEO controls the vote. But Tesla shareholders will be giving up any checks they previously had on Musk. When you combine that with the premium price both stocks currently trade at, it's hard to recommend buying either stock ahead of the potential merger.

    Energy Transfer (ET) is a diversified midstream energy tech giant with about 140,000 miles of pipelines and associated energy infrastructure in 44 states.     Sources indicate that recently, JPMorgan analyst Jeremy Tonet reiterated a buy rating on Energy Transfer stock and slightly raised his price target to $25 from $24. The analyst noted that the organization delivered a strong Q2 beat across all key metrics.

    According to recent reports, tonet highlighted that Energy Transfer raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $18.8 billion-$19.1 billion from $18.2 billion-$18.6 billion, reflecting robust base results and cost optimization.     Sources indicate that about the Hugh Brinson pipeline, Tonet noted Phase 1 (1.5 bcfd) reaching full capacity by September 1 and Phase II capacity (0.7 bcfd) going online by Q1 2027. The analyst also noted completion of a 14-mile Hugh Brinson lateral in Abilene, Texas, and final stages of talks for an additional 250 mmcfd of Oklahoma power plant demand.

    "All in, we see ET well positioned to continue capitalizing on organic growth opportunities across the value chain," mentioned Tonet.

    Industry observers note that tonet ranks No. 922 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 9%. See Energy Transfer Financials on TipRanks.

The company declared a base dividend of $0.16 per share for the third quarter, payable on September 30, 2026. At an annualized dividend of $0.64 per share, PR offers a yield of about 2.7%.

    Recently, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Permian Resources stock and increased his price target to $27 from $22, citing an improved outlook on oil production growth and operational efficiencies.

    The 5-star analyst noted that while PR stock has outperformed its peers so far in 2026, he sees further upside.     💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 5:15PM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Ford Motor Organization ›.
    • Industry observers note that as the transition to electric vehicles tests the resilience of legacy automakers, Ford Motor (F -0.62%) and General Motors (GM -3.72%) are racing to dominate the driveway.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 5:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Ford Motor Organization ›.

    Industry observers note that as the transition to electric vehicles tests the resilience of legacy automakers, Ford Motor (F -0.62%) and General Motors (GM -3.72%) are racing to dominate the driveway. Which stock is the better buy for your portfolio?

    In a recent development, ford is doubling down on its commercial segment through Ford Pro, while General Motors relies on a massive brand portfolio and its OnStar ecosystem to maintain loyalty. Both companies face the capital-intensive challenge of pivoting away from traditional engines. Comparing their financials and risk profiles helps determine which legacy giant is better positioned for the road ahead.

    Ford is restructuring its operations into three distinct units to better manage its evolution into a technology-led manufacturer. As a major player among consumer discretionary stocks, the company serves retail buyers through its gas-powered Ford Blue and electric Ford Model e segments. However, the Ford Pro division is a central pillar of its strategy, focusing on fleet optimization and telematics for commercial and government clients. This division provides a steady stream of recurring revenue from software services and maintenance for business fleets.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $187.0 billion, which represents a decrease of approximately 1.4% compared to the prior period. During this time, the automaker reported a net loss of close to $7.8 billion. This negative bottom-line result reflects the heavy costs associated with its aggressive capital investment strategy and the ongoing expenses of scaling its electric vehicle production. Despite the top-line dip, the firm continues to rely on its strong sales of high-margin trucks and commercial vans to support its broader business transformation.

    As of Sept. 30, 2026, Ford's debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 4.48x. This metric, which is total debt divided by shareholder equity, demonstrates the firm relies heavily on borrowed funds to fuel its operations. The current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term liabilities with short-term assets, stands at approximately 1.1x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was roughly $12.5 billion. This cash generation, defined as operating cash minus capital expenditures, helps provide the liquidity necessary to fund newly introduced vehicle platforms.

    It has been revealed that general Motors operates a diverse portfolio of iconic brands, including Chevrolet, Buick, GMC, and Cadillac, reaching customers in over 70 countries. The company focuses on maintaining high market share in the lucrative truck and SUV segments while simultaneously building out its Ultium battery platform. Beyond physical vehicles, the company leverages its OnStar connectivity service to create a digital ecosystem for both retail and fleet customers. This software-driven approach aims to improve customer retention and create upcoming high-margin revenue streams through connected services.

    According to recent reports, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $187.0 billion, a slight decrease of approximately 0.3% from the previous twelve months. Unlike its primary rival, the manufacturer remained profitable during this period, reporting net income of close to $4.0 billion. While revenue growth has been essentially flat, the ability to maintain positive net income demonstrates effective cost management across its traditional manufacturing base. This stability is vital as the company navigates the expensive transition toward a fully electric future.

    Recent findings suggest that as of Sept. 30, 2026, GM's debt-to-equity ratio was 2.0x. This ratio indicates the level of financial leverage the manufacturer uses, showing that its debt levels are lower relative to equity than those of its closest competitor. The current ratio is approximately 1.1x, indicating the firm has enough short-term assets to pay its upcoming bills. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $11.1 billion.

    Ford Motor faces significant operational risks, including potential supply chain disruptions for critical battery materials like lithium and cobalt. Quality control challenges that lead to expensive recalls and warranty costs also remain a persistent concern for the manufacturer. Furthermore, the tech giant must navigate a rapidly evolving electric vehicle market in China and increasing regulatory pressure regarding fuel economy standards. The capital-intensive nature of its current transformation plan means any significant slowdown in consumer demand could pressure its financial position.

    Recent findings suggest that general Motors remains heavily dependent on its high-margin internal combustion engine vehicles to fund its expensive shift toward electric and autonomous technology. The organization also faces high fixed costs from collective bargaining agreements and operational risks related to global supply chain dependencies. Additionally, recent legal settlements regarding the sale of driver data highlight ongoing cybersecurity and data privacy risks within its connected vehicle services. Scaling electric vehicle production to meet shifting consumer demand while competing with fresh software-driven entrants presents a major strategic hurdle.

    Ford appears slightly more attractive on a sales basis, though both companies trade at remarkably similar earnings multiples relative to their future earnings estimates.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    Sources indicate that I'd go with General Motors. It has turned its truck and SUV business into a dependable profit engine, and it is steadily bringing down the cost of its electric vehicle push.

    Here's what tipped it for me: Its North American business, the heart of the tech giant, is turning more of each sales dollar into operating profit year over year. GM also expects to generate well over $10 billion in cash this year, after covering its investments, and just approved a $20 billion share buyback, which gives each remaining share a bigger slice of the profits.

    According to recent reports, ford has a strong hand in commercial trucks and vans, where its Pro business is the company's biggest profit maker. But Ford expects 2027 earnings to merely match this year's, and its electric vehicle unit is still losing billions of dollars. GM's EV losses, meanwhile, are falling, with more improvement expected next year. For long-term investors, the strong truck profits, a lighter EV burden, and a substantial buyback tip the scales toward GM for 2027.

    Industry observers note that september ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

    In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Neocloud company CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

    Recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

    According to recent reports, chatterjee mentioned CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

    Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

    "CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," stated Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

    Recent findings suggest that chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

    Palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

    After a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

    Over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and upcoming markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security firm, Powell said. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

    Meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell said.

    BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

    Powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

    In a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he mentioned.

    It has been revealed that devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

    Additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

    According to recent reports, overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the organization if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he said. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

    "Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," said Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

    By RJ Fulton – Nov 22, 2026 at 5:20PM EST.

    Sources indicate that cryptocurrency markets demonstrated signs of stabilization on Sunday, November 22, following a brutal sell-off that triggered approximately $1.8 billion in forced liquidations across digital asset markets. As of early evening, Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) was up 1.15% to $60,785.36, while Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) gained 2.23% to $1,719.76. Solana (CRYPTO: SOL) lagged the broader market, edging 0.16% lower to $70.10. Despite the modest recovery, major cryptocurrencies remain under considerable pressure as investors assess whether the recent wave of forced selling has finally subsided.

    Industry observers note that the cryptocurrency market is attempting to stabilize following a sharp deterioration in global risk appetite that triggered widespread selling across equities, commodities, and digital assets. Friday's sell-off pushed Bitcoin to a two-year low near $55,000, while approximately $1.8 billion in leveraged cryptocurrency positions were liquidated as prices fell, forcing traders to unwind their exposure.

    Recent selling pressure across cryptocurrencies coincided with a broader retreat from risk assets as concerns over elevated valuations, persistently high interest rates, and tightening financial conditions weighed on investor sentiment. The simultaneous weakness across markets suggests investors prioritized cash and liquidity over rotating capital into safer investments.

    U.S.-listed spot cryptocurrency ETFs finished Friday's trading session with substantial losses. The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (NASDAQ: IBIT) declined 5.87%, while the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (NYSEMKT: FBTC) fell 6.16%. Meanwhile, the iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (NASDAQ: ETHA) plunged 9.16%.

    These figures reflect Friday's closing prices, as U.S. stock exchanges were closed over the weekend. With Bitcoin and Ethereum recovering from their recent lows, Monday's reopening will provide the first opportunity for these ETFs to reflect the latest weekend price movements during regular trading.

    The cryptocurrency market's modest recovery over the weekend offers some relief following last week's sharp sell-off, but it remains unclear whether the rebound reflects a meaningful improvement in investor demand or simply the exhaustion of forced selling. With leveraged positions liquidated during the downturn, the removal of excessive leverage could help stabilize prices. However, a sustainable recovery will require renewed buying interest rather than an absence of sellers.

    In a recent development, the reopening of U.S. equity markets on Monday will provide an key signal for investors. Cryptocurrencies have been particularly sensitive to weakness in technology stocks, and another round of selling across risk assets could quickly undermine the weekend's gains. Investors should monitor whether Bitcoin can sustain its recovery above $60,000, Ethereum can regain $1,800, and Solana can establish support above $70.

    Transfer insider Graeme Bailey recently claimed that there’s a strong chance of the veteran defender being offered at least a 12-month extension at Anfield, with Andoni Iraola unsurprisingly keen to keep hold of his skipper.

    In his latest Liverpool Confidential feature for the Daily Mail, Lewis Steele reported of fervent interest from Serie A in Van Dijk amid ongoing speculation over the centre-back’s future.

    The journalist wrote: ‘One source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides.

    While the Rossoneri appear determined to pounce on any uncertainty over Van Dijk’s future, Steele added that the 35-year-old is ‘keen’ to extend his contract at Liverpool.

    (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images).

    In a recent development, until such time that a final decision is communicated by LFC, fans’ nerves will be frayed as to Van Dijk’s future. When we’ve already seen Mo Salah and Andy Robertson depart this year, the loss of another modern-day great in 2027 would represent a further gut punch for Kopites.

    However, it’s worth remembering that when the Liverpool captain last penned a fresh contract in April 2025, he was just over two months away from leaving on a free, so he won’t panic even if there might be considerable gnashing of teeth outside of those involved in negotiations over his future.

    James Pearce recently advised Reds supporters not to expect a ‘quick resolution’ over the defender’s situation, so for now, it seems that the best way for Van Dijk to secure a newly introduced deal at Anfield is to maintain the strong performance levels he’s shown so far this season.

    The noise over his future is sure to continue for the time being, but we remain confident that everything will come together in due course and that our iconic number 4 will continue to grace the famous red shirt in the 2027/28 campaign.

    #119466. Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1031 w)

    Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1031 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
    • Industry observers note that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
    • The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

    Industry observers note that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

    The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

    Recent findings suggest that spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

    Industry observers note that the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

    Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," said Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

    It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he mentioned.

    Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

    "The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone said.

    He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

    That mentioned, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

    Industry observers note that "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

    While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

    In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, remarked Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

    "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she noted.

    In a recent development, the lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, stated Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

    Sources indicate that the overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he stated. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

    In addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

    The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she said.

    Sources indicate that "It is isolated," she mentioned. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

    For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

    "We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she said.

    Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

    But there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

    In a recent development, "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin said. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

    Recent findings suggest that it's also important to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, remarked R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

    "With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

    High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo noted.

    "That's when spreads really widen out," he said. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Rare-earth elements are key ingredients in high-strength permanent magnets that enable many of today's modern electronics, clean energy technologies, and defense applications, including drones and precision-guided munitions.
    • The United States is taking steps to create a domestically controlled "mine-to-magnet" supply chain as it looks to reduce its dependence on China, which controls 70% of rare-earth extraction and 90% of processing, according to a research report from The Motley Fool.
    • government is pouring money into rebuilding a rare-earth supply chain, and USA Rare Earth (USAR -8.73%) is one organization playing a key role in unlocking America's rare-earth industry.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Courtney Carlsen – Nov 22, 2026 at 5:30PM EST.

    Rare-earth elements are key ingredients in high-strength permanent magnets that enable many of today's modern electronics, clean energy technologies, and defense applications, including drones and precision-guided munitions.

    The United States is taking steps to create a domestically controlled "mine-to-magnet" supply chain as it looks to reduce its dependence on China, which controls 70% of rare-earth extraction and 90% of processing, according to a research report from The Motley Fool.

    The U.S. government is pouring money into rebuilding a rare-earth supply chain, and USA Rare Earth (USAR -8.73%) is one organization playing a key role in unlocking America's rare-earth industry. The company made several acquisitions to hit the ground running. But over the next five years, developing the Round Top mine in Texas will be key to its long-term success.

    Recent findings suggest that in recent years, the U.S. has taken a pivotal role in expanding the country's rare-earth supply chains by providing funds, investing in companies in the space, setting price floors, and acting as a guarantor to break China's stronghold.

    In June, the Department of Commerce finalized CHIPS Act funding of roughly $1.6 billion for USA Rare Earth, with $1.3 billion from senior secured loans and the remainder from grants.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    The funding supports its efforts to enter rare-earth mining and processing, including its acquisitions of Less Common Metals and Serra Verde Group, as well as the expansion of processing and magnet-making facilities in Oklahoma and South Carolina.

    In the coming years, USA Rare Earth will integrate its acquisitions, which help secure feedstock for rare-earth magnets while building out its U.S. manufacturing footprint. But a major part of its future lies in developing the Round Top deposit in West Texas.

    Recent findings suggest that the Round Top deposit is rich in heavy rare-earth elements (HREEs), which no U.S. mines at the moment produce at commercial scale. This would give USA Rare Earth a massive HREE supply, complementing its Serra Verde mine in Brazil, the largest-scale producer of HREEs outside Asia.

    Industry observers note that by owning the mine, factories, and processing, USA Rare Earth can capture margins across the entire value chain. The next five years are crucial for USA Rare Earth, and developing the Round Top project is a massive undertaking projected to cost around $1.4 billion. The company doesn't expect to begin commercial production at the Round Top until late 2028, with full-scale production coming by 2030.

    For investors seeking exposure to the U.S. rare-earth supply chain build-out, USA Rare Earth is a highly speculative, risky stock, especially as it incurs gigantic costs to integrate and expand its mine-to-magnet supply chain over the next several years.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Neil Patel – Nov 22, 2026 at 5:35PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Apple ›.

    It has been revealed that berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.47%) (BRKB -0.36%), under the direction of Warren Buffett, began buying Apple (AAPL -1.90%) shares in the first quarter of 2016. That investment has worked out extremely well. At one point, the Cupertino tech giant accounted for 50% of the conglomerate's portfolio.

    Even after trimming the position from fourth-quarter 2023 through the end of 2025, as of Nov. 17, the ”Magnificent Seven” stock represented 25% of Berkshire Hathaway's total public equity portfolio, and it is still its largest holding. The number of shares remained unchanged this year. This was despite there being a lot of shuffling among other positions.

    Here's what Berkshire holding on to the Apple stake tells investors.

    Recent findings suggest that over the three-month period from the start of July to the end of September, Apple shares traded at an average price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 36.8. Any rational investor would call this an expensive stock. That's doubly true for those who see equities through a value-focused lens. The share price has moved 29% higher in 2026.

    According to recent reports, berkshire Hathaway didn't sell a single share during the third quarter. This might come as a surprise to those who have followed the diversified corporation's actions in recent years.

    Warren Buffett oversaw the selling of Apple shares over multiple quarters from the end of 2023 to the end of 2025. For example, during the second quarter of 2024, when the technology stock traded at an average P/E multiple of 29, much lower than what it sells for today, Berkshire Hathaway cut its position dramatically.

    While the single holding had become a significant part of the portfolio, it's fair to assume that valuation played a part in these decisions. Now, with a P/E ratio that's approaching 40, it looks like less emphasis is being placed on the valuation being an influential factor.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Greg Abel has been the chief executive officer of Berkshire Hathaway since the start of 2026. He has made notable moves in his short tenure thus far, but as outside observers, we have zero clue what he and Warren Buffett are discussing regarding the conglomerate's capital allocation strategy. All we can do is try to come up with some takeaways.

    Staying true to Warren Buffett's investing philosophy, the Apple position is a clear signal that Berkshire Hathaway will hold on to its winners and let them run. "When we own portions of outstanding businesses with outstanding managements, our favorite holding period is forever," Buffett wrote in his 1988 shareholder letter.

    According to recent reports, the iPhone maker has been in the portfolio for nearly 11 years. Given how much of the market is driven by short-term behavior these days, that time horizon seems like an eternity.

    Sources indicate that if Berkshire Hathaway did sell some of its Apple shares in Q3, it wouldn't know where to move that capital. This is a persistent problem. Compared to the hundreds of billions of dollars on the balance sheet that earn low yields, an expensive Apple stock still offers the potential for higher returns. This benefits Berkshire Hathaway shareholders.

    Valuation should always be viewed separately from the underlying business. In this instance, Berkshire Hathaway's inactivity is a vote of confidence in the quality of Apple's operations.

    Sources indicate that it's hard to dispute that the consumer tech juggernaut is one of the finest companies we've ever seen. A valuable brand, ongoing pricing power, customer loyalty, and innovative DNA are attractive traits. There's also its incredible financial performance, shown by a fiscal 2026 free cash flow margin of 28%.

    Sources indicate that this isn't a sign for the average investor to go out and buy Apple stock. It is proof, however, that buying great businesses and leaving them alone can work wonders for your portfolio.

    Knicks' Mikal Bridges drills buzzer-beating 3-pointer to defeat Trail Blazers

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (427 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Newly introduced York Knicks are rounding into form, and maybe Saturday night is what Mikal Bridges needed to get back on track, too.
    • The 30-year-old wing, who came into a matchup with the Portland Trail Blazers shooting just north of 40% from the field and a smidge above 30% from deep, drilled a buzzer-beating 3-pointer to deliver Fresh York a 97-96 victory in Madison Square Garden.
    • According to recent reports, bridges finished with 12 points on 5-of-8 shooting.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Newly introduced York Knicks are rounding into form, and maybe Saturday night is what Mikal Bridges needed to get back on track, too.

    The 30-year-old wing, who came into a matchup with the Portland Trail Blazers shooting just north of 40% from the field and a smidge above 30% from deep, drilled a buzzer-beating 3-pointer to deliver Fresh York a 97-96 victory in Madison Square Garden.

    According to recent reports, bridges finished with 12 points on 5-of-8 shooting. He connected on two of his three attempts from long range. The last one extended the Knicks' win streak to four games.

    Following a pair of Deni Avdija free throws that put the Trail Blazers (10-6) up 96-94, New York (10-6) took a timeout. With 3.2 seconds remaining, Josh Hart inbounded the ball to Bridges.

    He caught the pass to the right of the top of the arc, used a quick fake to get an overzealous Toumani Camara to bite, took one more dribble and released.

    The ball rattled in, the buzzer sounded and Mike Breen exclaimed, "Bang! Bang!".

    Bridges was swarmed by his Knicks teammates, eventually wearing a smile as MSG reveled in utter pandemonium.

    Sources indicate that he came to the rescue on a night when Upcoming York squandered a 26-point lead. The Knicks shot 13 of 27 from 3-point land in the first half but scored only 31 points over the final two quarters.

    Bridges admitted afterward that Portland played "harder" than Newly introduced York in the second half.

    It has been revealed that but he also noted in that on-court postgame interview: "It's 48 minutes. We just kept persevering through the time and ended up winning the game.".

    Recent findings suggest that after trailing 94-84 with less than five minutes to go, the Trail Blazers went on a 12-0 run, which culminated in the aforementioned Avdija free throws. Additionally, that stretch featured a game-tying 3-pointer from Damian Lillard.

    Avdija was sent to the line because of a head-scratching foul by Knicks center Andre Drummond, who switched and committed the personal on the floor well beyond the arc.

    Avdija had 20 points. Center Donovan Clingan spearheaded Portland's effort with 22 points and 13 rebounds. Lillard put up just 15 points and shot a meager 1 of 9 from outside.

    In a recent development, fresh York was paced by Jalen Brunson's 30 points. Fellow guard Landry Shamet poured in 20 points.

    Bridges, though, was the hero, sinking a redemptive shot 16 games into what's been a trying season for the ninth-year pro.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 5:58PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Morningstar ›.

    Sources indicate that deciding between established financial research and high-growth payment technology requires a choice between steady market influence and rapid expansion. Is Morningstar (MORN -0.30%) or Sezzle (SEZL -6.09%) the better buy today?

    Morningstar provides the critical research and data that power modern investment decisions for millions of retail and institutional users. Conversely, Sezzle is a disruptor in the payments space, offering flexible financing options for younger consumers. While both operate in the financial world, they cater to different market segments with unique risk and reward profiles.

    Morningstar sells investment insights, data, and technology tools to a massive audience, including roughly 4.2 million individual investors and 425,000 financial advisors. The manufacturer serves eight primary customer groups, ranging from retirement plan providers and wealth managers to asset managers and fixed-income security issuers. Recently, it has integrated artificial intelligence through partnerships with major technology firms to automate analytics and improve user experience.

    Sources indicate that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $2.6 billion, representing revenue growth of approximately 9.4%. This expansion helped the organization achieve net income of close to $445.5 million during the same period. The steady climb in both top and bottom lines suggests consistent demand for the company's proprietary financial data and research services.

    It has been revealed that as of its September 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 1.8x (or 1.6x excluding operating lease liabilities). This ratio, which compares total debt to shareholder equity, reflects an increase in financial leverage after the manufacturer took on additional debt to fund acquisitions and share repurchases. The current ratio, which measures a company's ability to cover its short-term debts with short-term assets, is approximately 1.05x. In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $492.8 million (following $442.6 million in fiscal year 2025).

    It has been revealed that sezzle operates a platform that allows consumers to finance purchases at the point of sale. It focuses heavily on Gen Z and Millennial shoppers, connecting them with a vast network of merchants to increase average order values. By integrating with e-commerce platforms, the organization captures a growing slice of the fintech stocks landscape.

    Recent findings suggest that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $581.6 million, marking significant revenue growth of nearly 38.9%. This surge in activity led to a net income of close to $182.6 million for the period. The firm also maintained a strong net margin of roughly 31.4% during this high-growth phase, indicating it is generating significant profit from its revenue.

    As of its September 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio stands at approximately 4.2x, suggesting a robust ability to cover immediate liabilities. The debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.4x, meaning its total debt is less than half of its shareholder equity. In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $297.6 million, providing the company with substantial capital to reinvest in its growth and fund share repurchases.

    According to recent reports, morningstar faces risks tied to its reputation, as any perceived conflict of interest in its credit ratings or research could damage its brand. Its business is sensitive to market volatility, which can reduce asset-based fees when total market values decline. The company also competes with major data providers such as S&P Global (NYSE:SPGI) and MSCI (MSCI -2.22%) in the institutional research space.

    Sezzle relies heavily on a single originating bank partner, WebBank, for the majority of its loans, which creates a significant concentration risk. It faces intense competition in the payment sector and ongoing regulatory scrutiny regarding consumer lending practices and interest rates. Additionally, antitrust litigation involving partners like Shopify (SHOP -6.25%) could indirectly impact its growth trajectory or existing merchant relationships.

    Morningstar offers a more conservative entry point based on its sales, while Sezzle carries a higher premium that reflects its faster growth and superior net margin. The Forward P/E ratio compares a organization's share price to its future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    According to recent reports, but there are some risks that give me pause: Sezzle lends to shoppers, so bad loans matter. Its newest products start with higher losses, and regulators and a lawsuit against Shopify add costs and uncertainty.

    Morningstar, a trusted name in investing research, carries less credit risk, and its stock costs less relative to expected earnings. Its operating profit jumped last quarter, but sales growth is modest. Ultimately, I like that Sezzle is already profitable and still early in its expansion, with room to add latest services. If you're investing for the long haul and can handle some risk, Sezzle's fast-growing payments platform looks like the better buy for 2027.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Upstart's (UPST -7.88%) days as a hot fintech stock have long since passed.
    • While shares in this artificial intelligence (AI) lending technology company have seen brief partial rebounds in recent years, I’m looking more closely at fintech names with stronger growth stories, namely SoFi Technologies (SOFI -7.76%).
    • At first glance, it may seem illogical that Upstart continues to tumble.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Thomas Niel – Nov 22, 2026 at 6:04PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than SoFi Technologies ›.

    Upstart's (UPST -7.88%) days as a hot fintech stock have long since passed. It was trading near $400 per share back in 2021, but recently was changing hands for around $17 per share, a nearly 96% price decline.

    While shares in this artificial intelligence (AI) lending technology company have seen brief partial rebounds in recent years, I’m looking more closely at fintech names with stronger growth stories, namely SoFi Technologies (SOFI -7.76%).

    At first glance, it may seem illogical that Upstart continues to tumble. After all, following steep revenue declines in 2023 and 2024, sales and earnings have improved dramatically. In 2024, revenue and earnings per share (EPS) came in at $628.8 million and -$1.44, respectively. In 2025, revenue surged to just over $1 billion, with diluted EPS at $0.45 per share, marking a massive swing back to profitability.

    Sources indicate that for 2026, analysts' estimates call for Upstart to report $1.35 billion in sales and EPS of $1.84. Alas, there is a reason the market prices Upstart at such a low multiple to those estimates.

    First, there is high uncertainty over future growth. Although the tech giant recently reported a 34% increase in quarterly revenue to $371 million, and diluted earnings of $0.33 per share, up 43.4% from the prior year's quarter, management walked back its full-year guidance. Previously estimating  $1.4 billion in revenue and adjusted EBITDA of $294 million, Upstart's full-year 2026 outlook now calls for $1.32 billion in revenue and adjusted EBITDA of $260 million.

    According to recent reports, second, the recent pullback in AI stocks and tech stocks has likely intensified the situation. This sell-off has spilled over into the fintech space, including shares in SoFi, a company more richly priced than Upstart but with far greater long-term upside potential.

    Like Upstart, SoFi has recently reported strong growth. Last quarter, the digital-first financial services manufacturer reported net revenue of $1.4 billion, a 44% increase from the prior year's quarter. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 70% year over year, to $470 million. EPS came in at $0.18, a 63% increase from the $0.11 in diluted adjusted EPS reported for Q3 2025.

    Better yet, SoFi's management provided bullish guidance for the coming year. In 2027, the company anticipates 27% adjusted net revenue growth and adjusted earnings of $0.90 per share, adding that it could achieve these goals without raising additional capital. With SoFi Technologies changing hands today at around $13.50 per share, the stock is trading at around 15 times next year's estimated earnings.

    Recent findings suggest that longer-term, if SoFi can continue to grow at a moderate clip, steadily becoming a major "financial supermarket," shares could climb further, to past highs in the $30s per share, and beyond. Contrast that with Upstart, which, while still guiding for further growth, is revising that guidance downward. Worse yet, although both SoFi and Upstart are involved in the personal lending space, Upstart arguably has greater exposure. SoFi started as a lender but has since expanded into banking, brokerage, and other financial services, with its ability to cross-sell bolstering confidence in its growth story.

    It has been revealed that that remarked, it's still possible for Upstart to thrive while SoFi flounders. The sell-side remains divided on SoFi, perhaps reluctant to assign it a fintech valuation, given that it will eventually be classified as a bank stock. Upstart has tanked on poor guidance, but any sort of better-than-feared results and outlook could be enough to drive a relief rally. Nevertheless, if you're looking at either stock as a possible long-term investment rather than a trade, consider SoFi the better of the two.

"UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.

Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

    Furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the company's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

    Industry observers note that wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%.     Industry observers note that wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.
