He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

    Specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active users in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

    According to recent reports, "Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," said the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

    While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently launched Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the tech giant's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

    Morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

    Industry observers note that next is semiconductor organization Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

    After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

    The five-star analyst mentioned that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

    While XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the manufacturer raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

    Svanberg said that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

    According to recent reports, svanberg ranks No. 91 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 31.8%. See Marvell Technology Statistics on TipRanks.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Victor Wembanyama outscored the New Orleans Pelicans' starters in the first half on Saturday night at home.
    • By game's end, Wembanyama had scored 50 points, his second 50-point performance of the season, this time in a 114-91 victory over the Pelicans (5-13) at Frost Bank Center.
    • The 7-foot-4 superstar went for 52 points in a Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Victor Wembanyama outscored the New Orleans Pelicans' starters in the first half on Saturday night at home. He had 32 points. They had 26.

    By game's end, Wembanyama had scored 50 points, his second 50-point performance of the season, this time in a 114-91 victory over the Pelicans (5-13) at Frost Bank Center.

    The 7-foot-4 superstar went for 52 points in a Nov. 4 win over the Dallas Mavericks. Both of those outings have coincided with San Antonio (14-3) going 14-1 following an 0-2 start.

    It has been revealed that wembanyama, still only 22, has already tied Spurs legend David Robinson for the second-most 50-plus-point games in franchise history with three. George Gervin, a Basketball Hall of Famer like Robinson, leads the way with five.

    It has been revealed that wembanyama's got a long runway to surpass both Robinson and Gervin in that department. A third 50-piece this season would be historic in itself.

    He's the third player since 1973-74 to log at least 50 points, 15 rebounds and 5 blocks in a single game. Wembanyama clocked out after shooting 20 of 29 with 18 rebounds, 5 blocks and 4 steals.

    "It is very special," Wembanyama said, when asked about reaching the 50-point threshold in an on-court postgame interview.

    It has been revealed that he then said with a smile: "But unlike many of my peers, I'm not very good at stat padding. So I haven't reached it as many times as I should have.".

    Actress Selena Gomez was sitting courtside at the game. Wembanyama noticed.

    "Of course, I had to show off for Selena, you know," he mentioned, laughing.

    According to recent reports, the Spurs pulled away in the second quarter. San Antonio also got 19 points from guard Stephon Castle. Another backcourt contributor, De'Aaron Fox, piled up 10 assists.

    The Pelicans are 1-9 in their last 10 games. They've come undone after beginning the 2026-27 campaign with a 4-4 record. A bright spot for Upcoming Orleans is the continued growth of 20-year-old guard Jeremiah Fears, who led the team with 29 points in the loss.

    Recent findings suggest that as for Wembanyama, he's once again an NBA MVP candidate. It's looking like he'll face stiff competition for that award this season as well.

    Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić has a pair of 50-point games under his belt, too, and he's leading the league in scoring with 37.2 points per contest.

    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

    Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a organization's ability to pay dividends consistently.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The tech giant has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.

    In an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the firm's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

    Specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

    Sources indicate that furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in upcoming wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

    According to recent reports, "While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," said Mehta.

    Mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.

    Sources indicate that kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream company operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.

    Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst John Mackay reiterated a buy rating on Kinetik stock and slightly raised his price target to $58 from $57. He expects the manufacturer to report Q3 2026 EBITDA of $279 million, higher than the Street's expectation of $270 million but lower than the second quarter's EBITDA of $281 million.

    According to recent reports, the 5-star analyst expects Kinetik's Q3 performance to gain from higher gas volumes after notable curtailments in the second quarter. Mackay also expects the quarter to benefit from higher production and steady commodity margins, even though some lower-margin contracts and weaker Waha spread marketing gains could weigh on results.

    Overall, Mackay increased his Q3 2026 estimates to reflect higher volumes, driven by rapid Permian egress pipeline commissioning, stronger throughput at Kings Landing I, and higher M2M commodity prices, offset by increased costs.

    "As natural gas takeaway constraints ease across the Permian, investor focus centers on KNTK's YE26 volume trajectory and durability of its multi-year growth," said Mackay.

    Recent findings suggest that mackay ranks No. 569 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.9%. See Kinetik's Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Industry observers note that moving to Crescent Energy (CRGY), an exploration and production company with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian, and Uinta Basins. With a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share (annualized dividend of $0.48 per share), CRGY's dividend yield stands at 3.56%. Earlier this month, Crescent declared an agreement to acquire Eagle Ford assets from Devon Energy (DVN).

    Recent findings suggest that heading into Q3 earnings on Nov. 2, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reiterated a buy rating on Crescent stock and slightly lowered the price target to $17 from $18, citing dilution from new shares.

    "CRGY's recent acquisition of DVN's Eagle Ford assets marks a strategic, growth-oriented move, potentially enhancing cash flow performance," mentioned Richardson.

    The 5-star analyst noted that the acquisition of the Eagle Ford assets at a net purchase price of $3.85 billion will add about 68 MBoe/d of net production and over 600 net Tier 1 locations. Richardson added that a solid track record of synergies from past deals in the Eagle Ford region increases confidence about Crescent achieving efficiencies with this deal.

    Additionally, Richardson noted that the financial implications of the acquisition seem impressive, with a projected increase in cash flow per share of about 9% for 2027 to 2029.

    The analyst believes that Crescent is not just expanding its business through acquisitions but positioning itself as a more durable firm, regardless of market conditions.

    Richardson ranks No. 478 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Crescent Energy Statistics on TipRanks.

    #119419. Europe's cyber weak spot is the everyday businesses nobody thought to protect

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1017 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Europe's cyber weak spot is the everyday businesses nobody thought to protect

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1017 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, cyberattacks on refrigerators in French supermarkets in October spurred Swedish chain Coop to act.
    • Attackers hit refrigeration systems in seven of its stores in early November.
    • Mundane but essential equipment, used by everyday businesses, has become a favorite target of cyber saboteurs in recent weeks.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, cyberattacks on refrigerators in French supermarkets in October spurred Swedish chain Coop to act. But it wasn't fast enough.

    Attackers hit refrigeration systems in seven of its stores in early November. The affected stores had been scheduled for security upgrades just two days later, a company spokesperson told CNBC.

    Mundane but essential equipment, used by everyday businesses, has become a favorite target of cyber saboteurs in recent weeks.

    Experts are warning that a combination of known vulnerabilities, basic security failures and ambiguity over whether suppliers or their clients are responsible are making things worse, as AI makes cyber threats faster and more sophisticated.

    Guy Segal, CEO of cybersecurity firm Sygnia, told CNBC that his tech giant handled 285% more incidents in October than a year earlier, with demand forcing it to turn away some businesses seeking emergency assistance.

    "It's going to get worse before it's going to get better," Segal remarked.

    The recent cyberattacks targeted refrigeration systems across hundreds of European supermarkets, remotely altering temperature settings and forcing retailers to discard spoiled food.

    France has since accused a cyber unit with links to Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps of the attacks, an allegation Tehran denies.

    Fredrik Blix, a cybersecurity researcher at Stockholm University, told CNBC that thousands of industrial control systems remain accessible over the public internet, sometimes despite manufacturers' warnings.

    Segal mentioned that basic cyber protection measures such as multi-factor authentication and basic network segmentation are more crucial than ever.

    He stated risks to major civic infrastructure like the electrical grid were front of mind and so "usually pretty well protected.".

    Industry observers note that "There are always those civil supply chain components that are way, way less protected. Could be supermarkets, could be gas stations, could be… the screens on the Tube," Segal noted, referring to London's underground rail system.

    The supermarket attacks indicated "this is the newly introduced normal, and definitely it's a wake-up call for every company out there," Segal added.

    Segal mentioned that inexpensive AI tools mean technical expertise and resources are no longer needed to launch attacks. He described one recent incident in which clients suffered breaches within six hours of a vulnerability becoming known, as perpetrators used AI to act faster — a process that might have taken weeks a year earlier.

    Segal, whose firm helps companies respond to breaches and strengthen their defenses, warned that businesses without prearranged incident-response support could struggle to secure emergency assistance, as overwhelmed cybersecurity firms prioritize existing clients.

    In one case, he said, Sygnia had to turn down a tech giant because no response teams were available. Segal added that the company in question had already been turned down by ten other providers.

    Jacob Silverman, CEO of risk advisory firm Kroll, told CNBC earlier this month that the company was operating at full capacity in its incident-response business amid what he described as "the most rapid uptick in threat activity that we've ever seen.".

    Segal argued that retailers should treat cybersecurity risks with the same seriousness as fire safety and food hygiene, including when outsourcing maintenance.

    Industry observers note that when Ahold Delhaize stores in Belgium and Luxembourg were attacked on Nov. 2, it exposed how different independent store operators had responded to the warnings following the earlier attacks in France.

    Retailers had been warned about the vulnerabilities following earlier attacks in France, and those that implemented the recommended protections were spared, CEO Frans Muller told investors in an earnings call earlier this month, but smaller operators with fewer technical resources had struggled to make the necessary changes.

    Coop, whose stores are owned by regional consumer cooperatives or operated by franchises, told CNBC that public attention on the recent attacks was the main driver of security improvements. It noted the vulnerability at the affected stores had since been addressed.

    The financial consequences of cyberattacks can be substantial. Ahold Delhaize told investors in November that a separate October cyberattack on its online operations and supply chain would reduce fourth-quarter sales by 200 million euros ($219 million).

    Danish shipping giant Maersk, which suffered an estimated $250 million to $300 million in losses from the 2017 NotPetya cyberattack, has spent nearly a decade strengthening its defenses.

    CEO Vincent Clerc told CNBC earlier this month that the experience had prompted significant investment in security capabilities, but warned that AI was enabling attackers to become more effective.

    "Everybody is in a race" to boost defenses, he said.

    According to recent reports, research by cybersecurity firm Censys found that the number of internet-exposed refrigeration controllers made by Danfoss and Copeland exposed to cyber hacking fell 53% globally between Oct. 9 and Nov. 5.

    However, more than 3,100 remained exposed, and Censys said it could not determine whether the decline reflected permanent security improvements or equipment simply being taken offline.

    A Copeland spokesperson confirmed that some of its refrigeration systems were affected by the vulnerability and stated it had contacted customers to reinforce cybersecurity guidance, including keeping devices off the public internet and updating software.

    Danfoss didn't respond to CNBC requests for comment.

    In a recent development, in the U.K., a covert cybersecurity operation has been underway to protect tens of thousands of refrigeration systems at supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants and other businesses, the BBC reported on Friday. After researchers discovered a major vulnerability in late October, cybersecurity specialists, IT teams and the U.K.'s National Cyber Security Centre worked to alert dozens of companies and secure their systems before hackers could exploit the flaw.

    The EU's Cyber Resilience Act will also impose stricter security requirements on manufacturers of connected products from December 2027.

    But the legislation does not require all existing equipment to be made compliant with the latest standards.

    Blix told CNBC on Nov. 6 that European authorities should take a more proactive approach to reducing vulnerabilities by identifying exposed industrial control systems and contacting their operators before attacks occur.

    "What worries me is that we don't really do anything," he said, adding that "we are shuffling a lot of papers" and "doing a lot of risk assessments" but failing to take meaningful action.

    • Now, only Hall of Famers Antonio Gates, with 118, and Tony Gonzalez, with 115, sit ahead of Kelce.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Travis Kelce finally jumped Rob Gronkowski on Sunday afternoon.

    Kelce hauled in an 8-yard touchdown early in the Kansas City Chiefs' 34-7 blowout win over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. That marked the 109th score of Kelce's career, which moved him to third on the NFL's all-time touchdown list by a tight end and broke a tie with Gronkowski. The longtime Upcoming England Patriots star finished his career with 108 touchdowns.

    Now, only Hall of Famers Antonio Gates, with 118, and Tony Gonzalez, with 115, sit ahead of Kelce.

    It has been revealed that kelce scored again in the second quarter when Patrick Mahomes found him for a 22-yard touchdown. Kelce jumped up and made the grab between a trio of Cardinals.

    That touchdown put the Chiefs up 23-7 at the time.

    Kelce finished the game with 74 receiving yards on six receptions in the 27-point win, which pushed the Chiefs to 8-2 on the season. Mahomes went 27-of-39 passing for 324 yards with three touchdowns. He sat early in the fourth quarter with the win all but secured. The Cardinals (3-8) have lost three straight.

    Recent findings suggest that sunday was also Kelce's 100th regular-season game at Arrowhead Stadium, which made him the fourth player in team history to reach that mark. Kelce has already broken the NFL record for most yards after catch in league history this season, too, and earlier this fall Mahomes and Kelce surpassed Gates and Philip Rivers for the most yards generated by a tight end and quarterback duo in NFL history.

    Kelce has spent his entire career with the Chiefs, who first selected him out of Cincinnati in the third round of the 2013 NFL Draft. He has 13,588 receiving yards in his career, which trails only Gonzalez among tight ends, and he has 586 receiving yards and four touchdowns this season.

    While Kelce's career is winding down, he is only nine touchdowns shy of becoming the all-time tight end touchdown leader. That may be tough to pull off with just seven games left in the regular season, but the mark is in reach.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
    • Recent findings suggest that here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept.
    • It has been revealed that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    Recent findings suggest that here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    It has been revealed that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    Sources indicate that robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the tech giant has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    It has been revealed that transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    It has been revealed that net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    So much for buying the dip.As the S&P 500 entered correction territory and the Nasdaq-100 flirted with bear-market territory, down 19% from highs as of midday Friday, the single biggest options trade of the day was a near $100-million bet that the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) has a long way more to fall.Around 12:30 E.T., someone spent $93 million buying 20,000 380-strike puts expiring Sep. 17, 2027, according to trading data reviewed by SpotGamma and Volland, options-analytics platforms that both show the trade as a likely opening position, with volume exceeding existing open interest in the contract. The trade bets that the index will fall below $380, a nearly 8% decline from its current level. The SMH is off 40% from its recent all-time highs.

    Sources indicate that "That trade stands out big-time," wrote Jason DeLorenzo, founder and owner of Volland. "It is either a hedge or speculative, but either way it isn't a vote of confidence."The puts were bought for $46.50 a piece, an arguably expensive choice for a downside bet with volatility in the ETF trading at 70.

    In a recent development, "You're paying a metric ton of Vega for that thing," added SpotGamma's Brent Kochuba, referring to the contract's sensitivity to changes in volatility of the underlying chip ETF. "Maybe they were a forced buyer, or maybe they're actually selling this, which can still be the case even though the price indicates it happening closer to the ask.".

    The semiconductor index headed for a 9% drop this week alone.

    #119400. Ravens doomed by 4 turnovers vs. Panthers, including fumble through end zone in back-and-forth thriller

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (633 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Ravens doomed by 4 turnovers vs. Panthers, including fumble through end zone in back-and-forth thriller

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (633 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Justice Hill thought he had a touchdown Sunday against the Carolina Panthers.
    • Instead, the Baltimore Ravens running back fumbled through the end zone to spark a wild sequence of events that ultimately resulted in a score for the Panthers.
    • The sequence proved critical as the Panthers went on to a 35-33 win that was sealed by a go-ahead Panthers field goal followed up by a Jacoby Brissett interception.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Justice Hill thought he had a touchdown Sunday against the Carolina Panthers.

    Instead, the Baltimore Ravens running back fumbled through the end zone to spark a wild sequence of events that ultimately resulted in a score for the Panthers.

    The sequence proved critical as the Panthers went on to a 35-33 win that was sealed by a go-ahead Panthers field goal followed up by a Jacoby Brissett interception.

    In a recent development, with the win, the Panthers improved to 5-5 to increase their lead in the NFC South to two games over the rest of the division. The Bucs, Falcons and Saints are all 3-7.

    With 12:17 remaining in the second quarter and Baltimore holding a 12-7 lead, Hill took a handoff from the Carolina 37-yard line and broke free through the secondary toward the end zone. But just before he reached the end zone, Carolina cornerback Will Lee punched the ball out of of Hill's grasp.

    The ball then bounced through the end zone to trigger perhaps the most controversial rule in football. Even though the Panthers didn't recover the loose ball, they took over possession via a touchback.

    Just like that, a would-be Ravens score turned into a turnover at the last moment thanks to a heads-up play from Lee.

    Industry observers note that the Panthers didn't initially do much with their good fortune. They punted after a 3-and-out on their ensuing possession. But another Ravens miscue set them up with another opportunity.

    This time, LaJohntay Wester muffed the punt return, allowing the Panthers to recover deep in Baltimore territory.

    Industry observers note that this time, the Panthers capitalized. Two plays later, Chuba Hubbard ran 18 yards around the left edge for a touchdown and a 14-12 Carolina lead.

    All was not lost for the Ravens in the wild sequence.

    The very next touch for the Ravens resulted in a score. Devontez Walker returned the ensuing kickoff 86 yards for a touchdown to put the Ravens back on top with a 19-14 lead.

    If you're counting, that's three consecutive Ravens touches that resulted in a fumble through the end zone, a muffed punt that led to a Carolina touchdown and a kickoff return for a Baltimore touchdown.

    Industry observers note that but Baltimore's lead would not hold. The lead changed hands five more times from there in a back-and-forth battle that gave Panthers fans in Charlotte their money's worth.

    According to recent reports, the teams exchanged two more touchdowns before halftime, and the Ravens went into the break with a 26-22 advantage. Carolina then opened the second half with a touchdown for a 29-26 lead that that the Ravens took back on a 15-yard Derrick Henry touchdown run with 6:32 remaining.

    That left Carolina with the ball and a 33-32 deficit.

    Bryce Young led a 12-play, 55-yard drive from there to set up Ryan Fitzgerald for a 37-yard field goal and a 35-33 Panthers lead with 1:44 remaining. From there, Tyrel Dodson iced the win with an interception of Brissett.

    Brissett evaded pressure on the first-and-10 play from the Baltimore 32. But he threw an ill-advised pass off his back foot that resulted in a batted ball in the secondary that Dodson caught.

    In a recent development, the late interception encapsulated a day in which the Panthers secured a 4-1 advantage in takeaways. Henry lost a fumble in addition to the turnovers by Brissett, Hill and Wester. The Ravens out-gained the Panthers in total offensive yardage, 421 to 378, but their miscues ultimately cost them the game.

    The Ravens also lost Henry to injury. He left the field after his fourth-quarter touchdown for concussion evaluation. His status wasn't immediately clear postgame.

    The loss drops a disappointing Ravens team to 4-7, well out of the AFC playoff picture.

    #119391. Why Anthropic's blockbuster IPO couldn't escape the stock market correction

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1287 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Why Anthropic's blockbuster IPO couldn't escape the stock market correction

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1287 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • No one can say the Anthropic initial public offering wasn't a success for the company.
    • The Anthropic IPO reinforces those fears rather than running counter to them, claims Avery Marquez, director of investment strategies at Renaissance Capital, which researches IPOs and manages the Renaissance IPO ETF (IPO).
    • "The volatility in the AI trade we've been seeing for the past few months stems from valuations and whether we are in a bubble, and that's been heightened and highlighted by the Anthropic IPO," Marquez remarked on "ETF Edge" on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    No one can say the Anthropic initial public offering wasn't a success for the company. Deal size and pricing were signs of what IPO experts say was insatiable demand for "ANT" shares. But what came within a day is something that investors better get used to: anxiety in the stock market about valuations being assigned to artificial intelligence revenue and business models that should keep Anthropic shares volatile in the period ahead.

    The Anthropic IPO reinforces those fears rather than running counter to them, claims Avery Marquez, director of investment strategies at Renaissance Capital, which researches IPOs and manages the Renaissance IPO ETF (IPO).

    "The volatility in the AI trade we've been seeing for the past few months stems from valuations and whether we are in a bubble, and that's been heightened and highlighted by the Anthropic IPO," Marquez remarked on "ETF Edge" on Friday.

    And in the case of Anthropic, which finished trading Friday down 9%, the valuation anxiety becomes "so much more prevalent," she added, because it is a upcoming stock.

    It is not just any latest stock, but one that has Wall Street adding downside risks to research notes likely never seen before, and which may be the greatest understatement (or most subtle equities research joke) in the history of earnings analysis. "Anthropic could develop AI systems which become fully autonomous and wipe out humanity which may lead to a serious decline in earnings," Seaport Research Partners analyst wrote Jay Goldberg wrote on Nov. 18.

    "It was challenging manufacturer to value ... and it's very richly valued," Marquez said. "We're seeing something more reasonable and investors grappling now with where should this company actually be valued," she added.

    In a recent development, the fact that Anthropic pulled off the deal in this market and was able to command the price it did was an achievement, according to Yuri Khodjamirian, chief investment officer at Tema ETFs, which offers multiple funds that invest in pre-IPO shares of companies and held Anthropic in its Tema Photonics & Optical ETF (LAZR) well before IPO day. "We have to remember they pulled off a very large IPO in the middle of a very severe market with the volatility in the tech sector specifically," Khodjamirian said on "ETF Edge.".

    Sources indicate that khodjamirian states the investor demand for AI remains, but amid a reassessment of returns. And he says an equally hard task has now begun for Anthropic. Investors are unwinding positions in everything from tech stocks to gold and bitcoin, and repositioning for 2027 based on their latest outlooks. "We are in a bit of vacuum," he said.

    "From here on the market is trying trying to figure out what direction to go in," Khodjamirian stated, whether that is based on Fed policy, geopolitics, the midterm elections results, or the AI trade. "In many cases, the chief investment officers I speak to, and the clients, say 'I'm just gonna take some risk off and wait and see until I get more info.' And with the Anthropic, the revenue picture and how the AI adoption curve progresses will be a vital stat to watch," he added.

    Industry observers note that plenty of value has already been wiped out in tech, according to Khodjamirian, but investors need latest signals to buy. That doesn't just go for Anthropic but for much of the market's tech leadership. "One of the things most difficult for investors to understand right now is some of the leadership in the market that has been taken by semiconductor companies," he mentioned, adding that the peak was 22% of S&P 500 earnings. But these companies, like Nvidia and Micron, have a very different earnings profile from the rest of the market.

    According to recent reports, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH), which was down over 10% on Friday and around 15% for the week, was on pace for its worst week since September 2001, according to CNBC data on Friday afternoon. It also lost 15% in one week of March 2020. The tech sector of the S&P 500, tracked by the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK), turned in its worst weekly performance since the Covid crash.

    Khodjamirian mentioned while these stocks may look cheap on a P/E basis right now after the heavy selling, that requires faith in the earnings estimates, which he says will be more notable as results are released for the next few years. "Right now it looks cheap, but will companies like Micron and Nvidia actually deliver?".

    Nvidia shares fell 14% on Friday, adding to its worst stretch of weekly performance since 2008. What's more, the single biggest trade in the options market on Friday was a near $100-million bet that the VanEck Semiconductor ETF has a long way more to fall.

    And the same caution about the outlook goes for Anthropic, he said. "That's why we need to watch Anthropic's annual recurring revenue number, because it is a key part of puzzle," he said.

    Recent findings suggest that marquez stated there is always hype in names like SpaceX and Anthropic when they go public, and it is hard to know whether the pricing of the deal is based on fundamentals, "but we just need more time and lots price discovery," she said. "It is not going to happen overnight," she added.

    In a recent development, as an IPO researcher, she states this "discernment" is a healthy thing for the markets. There are few cases to look to as comps for Anthropic, other than SpaceX, and before that, way back to Facebook's IPO in 2012. And neither example is one of quick recovery. SpaceX shares remain well below their first-day closing price more than five months after its IPO. Facebook (now Meta), meanwhile, "did not do well for the first year after going public and we see where it is now. It's just the nature of these disruptive tech companies that come to market," Marquez said. "They lend themselves to more volatility and a longer period of price discovery for investors.".

    Industry observers note that all eyes will next be on Anthropic's rival OpenAI, which has suggested it will be ready to go public in 2027. Marquez noted the reaction to the Anthropic deal may be a signal that it was "a good idea to wait, allowing themselves to build more quarters of better financials and improve fundamentals a bit before taking on a market that is really quite discerning.".

    Tema does not own shares of OpenAI in any of its ETFs. But, "I can't say it wont be," Khodjamirian mentioned. "They exist out there in the secondary market, and we will look at it, but we haven't made any decision. It depends on the ETF fit and if the portfolio manager wants to invest. We are always looking out for these interesting businesses but never just for the sake of private exposure," he added.

    Recent findings suggest that tema does own Databricks, Stripe, Kalshi and Polymarket across its funds. It also was an investor in SpaceX pre-IPO through its Tema Space Innovators ETF (NASA).

    According to recent reports, khodjamirian mentioned demand from public market investors to access these "generational businesses" will continue to be the case, despite the market volatility, and will more often come before IPO day. In fact, he pointed to the filing from the world's largest asset manager and one of the biggest ETF companies in the world, BlackRock, earlier this week. It wants to bring out a new kind of exchange-traded product that would bring the ETF and interval fund structures together as a way to increase exposure to private companies, with shares trading on an exchange while the fund makes monthly repurchase offers.

    #119387. An early breakdown in the polar vortex is threatening already depleted gas stocks

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (754 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    An early breakdown in the polar vortex is threatening already depleted gas stocks

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (754 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • An unprecedented early breakdown of the stratospheric polar vortex and a record-breaking El Niño event has put energy traders on alert this winter, with analysts warning the weather and climate phenomena could have an outsized impact on Europe.
    • Meteorologists are currently observing a record early breakdown of the polar vortex, a large-scale circulation of strong winds that typically keeps extremely cold air over the North Pole.
    • Changes in the strength and shape of the polar vortex can influence weather patterns much lower down in the atmosphere, potentially bringing in colder weather to parts of Europe and North America.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An unprecedented early breakdown of the stratospheric polar vortex and a record-breaking El Niño event has put energy traders on alert this winter, with analysts warning the weather and climate phenomena could have an outsized impact on Europe.

    Meteorologists are currently observing a record early breakdown of the polar vortex, a large-scale circulation of strong winds that typically keeps extremely cold air over the North Pole.

    Changes in the strength and shape of the polar vortex can influence weather patterns much lower down in the atmosphere, potentially bringing in colder weather to parts of Europe and North America.

    This year, however, the collapse of the stratospheric polar vortex, or SPV, is taking place at the same time as an unusually powerful El Niño, a climate event that can boost global temperatures and disrupt rainfall.

    In a recent development, the collision of these two events raises the risk of a prolonged cold spell that could lift heating demand and force European countries to draw down already-low reserves faster. That would leave the continent more reliant on imported liquefied natural gas (LNG) at a time when supplies from the Middle East are disrupted.

    To be sure, Europe's natural gas storage levels started the winter at their lowest level in more than a decade.

    The International Energy Agency warned earlier this month that low European storage levels and limited storage options in several LNG-importing countries in Asia and South America could intensify the competition for cargoes and put upward pressure on prices during periods of high demand.

    Simon Lee, a lecturer in atmospheric science at the U.K.'s University of St Andrews, said the combination of a sudden stratospheric warming (SSW) with an El Niño event is not necessarily unusual, but meteorologists had been expecting a polar vortex breakdown in February — not as early as November.

    The early SPV disruption is an "extremely rare" event that could influence winter weather in northwest Europe and the eastern U.S., Lee said, increasing the chance of colder conditions although likely not to the extent that a polar vortex event caused parts of Niagara Falls to partially freeze in January 2014.

    "Geopolitics and weather are the two key volatility drives for energy and now they seem to be happening at the same time — and that's always the biggest risk for markets," Florence Schmit, senior energy strategist at Rabobank, told CNBC.

    For months, meteorologists expected an El Niño event would result in a milder winter in Europe and relatively muted heating demand, Schmit remarked, which was broadly seen as welcome news given ongoing concerns over the continent's tight regional supplies for gas and crude oil.

    According to recent reports, the prospect of a colder-than-expected winter due to an early breakdown of the polar vortex could be "incredibly difficult" for Europe to navigate, Schmit warned. She noted that the region's gas storages have seen "very, very strong withdrawals" over the last two weeks, "which is quite unusual for this time of year.".

    "If you continue to see the same storage withdrawals over the next couple of months, that means energy prices will spike again — and they won't spike because of geopolitics. This time it will be the weather driving that spike and that volatility," Schmit mentioned.

    European gas prices have soared to levels not seen since the 2022 energy crisis in recent weeks, notching 103.9 euros ($113.99) per megawatt hour in late October. European benchmark Dutch TTF futures for December delivery stood at around 87.28 euros on Friday afternoon.

    "We have never seen an early breakdown of the polar vortex and a super el Nino in the same winter so we have no historical precedent on how this will impact global gas demand," David Lewis, principal research analyst of gas and liquified natural gas at Wood Mackenzie, told CNBC by email.

    El Niño is commonly associated with milder winters, while a SSW event typically leads to colder temperatures and higher snowfall, Lewis mentioned, noting this could materialize in December and January within Europe.

    "So far, the start of the European winter heating season has been quite cold but more importantly has seen low wind speeds across Northern Europe," Lewis stated.

    Industry observers note that "The drawdown in stocks in the first half of November has been amongst the highest on record. With inventories starting the winter at their lowest level on record, any further deterioration in temperatures or wind speeds will have an outsized impact on European balances and lead to higher prices across Europe," he added.

    Eagles QB Joe Milton III stood and watched his fumble in shades of infamous Cam Newton Super Bowl play. Then he delivered late to beat the Steelers

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (467 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Philadelphia quarterback Joe Milton III made an early play to draw the ire of Eagles fans Sunday.
    • He finished with a big throw to help secure a 19-16 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers and snap a seven-game losing streak.
    • Industry observers note that milton made his second start for the Eagles Sunday in place of the benched Tanner McKee and sidelined starter Jalen Hurts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Philadelphia quarterback Joe Milton III made an early play to draw the ire of Eagles fans Sunday.

    He finished with a big throw to help secure a 19-16 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers and snap a seven-game losing streak.

    Industry observers note that milton made his second start for the Eagles Sunday in place of the benched Tanner McKee and sidelined starter Jalen Hurts. He did not do his best to make a good early impression on the home fans.

    On Philadelphia's second play from scrimmage, Milton was stripped of the ball in the backfield by Steelers pass rusher Alex Highsmith. But it wasn't the fumble that's likely to draw the ire of Eagles fans. It was his response to the loose ball.

    Milton wasn't tackled on the play. And as the ball hit the ground near his feet, he just stood there and looked at it.

    Milton made no effort to secure the loose ball that he had a chance at recovering.

    Fortunately for the Eagles, left tackle Jordan Mailata did make a play on the ball and was able to secure it before Highsmith could. It was a good break for the Eagles that could go a long way in saving Milton from heat in Philadelphia.

    The Eagles were able to convert the recovery into an early 3-0 lead.

    Industry observers note that the early field goal helped the Eagles to a 13-0 first-quarter lead. Philadelphia's defense did the work from there, holding the Steelers out of the end zone until the final two minutes of the game.

    But the game wasn't quite over after the late Steelers score. Philadelphia got the ball back with 1:21 remaining with a 3-point lead in need of a first down to secure the win. Milton delivered with a 7-yard completion to Devonta Smith on third-and-6 to ice the win.

    Milton finished the game completing 11-of-21 passes for 141 yards without a touchdown or an interception.

    In a recent development, the first-quarter play drew immediate visions of Cam Newton. The former Carolina Panthers great made — or didn't make — a famously familiar play with considerably higher stakes attached.

    With his Panthers trailing the Denver Broncos by six points in the fourth quarter of Super Bowl 50, Newton was stripped of the ball by Broncos pass rusher Von Miller.

    Like Milton on Sunday, Newton had a shot at recovering the ball and made no effort to do so. But Newton's Panthers weren't as fortunate as the Eagles on Sunday.

    The Broncos recovered Newton's fumble deep in Carolina territory to help seal a 24-10 Denver win.

    According to recent reports, milton's lack of effort clearly won't go down in infamy like Newton's. And he found himself in the good graces of Eagles fans by game's end.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Zscaler shares surged 18% in extended trading on Friday after Bloomberg reported that CrowdStrike is in talks to buy the cybersecurity vendor. Shares of CrowdStrike shares fell more than 8%.

    The talks between the two companies are ongoing, Bloomberg reported, citing sources familiar in the matter. CrowdStrike declined to comment on the report. Zscaler didn't immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.

    CrowdStrike has been one of the big cybersecurity winners in the artificial intelligence boom, with its stock about doubling in value this year, lifting its market cap to $235 billion. Zscaler, meanwhile, is down 13% this year, pushing its market cap down to about $32 billion.

    Along with CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks has seen its business boom as businesses race to upgrade their networks in the AI era. Palo Alto closed Friday at a nearly $282 billion market cap.

    Should a deal take place, it would be among the largest in the history of the cybersecurity industry. Google acquired Wiz last year for $32 billion. In 2024, Cisco paid about $28 billion for Splunk. Earlier this year, Palo Alto closed its purchase of CyberArk for $25 billion.

    CrowdStrike's deals to this point have been on the smaller side.The firm unveiled prepares earlier this month to acquire agentic observability platform Fiddler AI and AI trust platform Dreadnode.

    #119374. DK Metcalf ejected after another dustup with Eagles' Cooper DeJean, unsportsmanlike conduct penalty amid Steelers loss

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (729 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    DK Metcalf ejected after another dustup with Eagles' Cooper DeJean, unsportsmanlike conduct penalty amid Steelers loss

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (729 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf had more costly penalties on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field than receptions.
    • Recent findings suggest that metcalf was ejected with only one reception to his name after the second of those infractions late in the third quarter during a 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
    • Industry observers note that he was called for taunting in the wake of his latest dustup with Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf had more costly penalties on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field than receptions.

    Recent findings suggest that metcalf was ejected with only one reception to his name after the second of those infractions late in the third quarter during a 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. The final straw was when he was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct.

    Industry observers note that he was called for taunting in the wake of his latest dustup with Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean. And so Metcalf, who was notably suspended two games last season for swinging at a Detroit Lions fan during a sideline altercation, was disqualified, with Philly fans waving goodbye to him as he walked to the tunnel.

    The taunting penalty occurred in the fallout of a third-and-8 incompletion from Aaron Rodgers with less than five minutes left in the third quarter. Rodgers was looking for wide receiver Germie Bernard toward the left pylon. Metcalf was lined up on the right side of the field pre-snap, in the slot, where he was matched up with DeJean.

    According to recent reports, following the play, the CBS Sports broadcast demonstrated Metcalf and Philadelphia safety Marcus Epps getting into it. Metcalf had to be restrained by Pittsburgh wide receiver Roman Wilson and tight end Pat Freiermuth.

    After Metcalf walked off to the sideline, however, the broadcast displayed another clip that exhibited Metcalf putting his hand into DeJean's face mask. DeJean appeared to indicate that he was poked in the eye.

    Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy confirmed that accusation postgame, explaining that the referee told him that Metcalf "poked the defender in the eye.".

    In a recent development, not only was Metcalf DQ'd, but he also lost his team 15 yards. That backed up a Chris Boswell field-goal attempt, which ended up being from 52 yards out. Fortunately for Pittsburgh, Boswell still made the kick to cut the team's deficit to 16-9.

    But, even with some help from little-known wideout Max Hurleman in Metcalf's absence — the former undrafted free agent hauled in a late touchdown after being elevated from the practice squad — the Steelers (6-4) fell by three points.

    In turn, the injury-ravaged Eagles (3-7) snapped their seven-game losing streak.

    Afterward, McCarthy was asked about his confidence level in Metcalf.

    "I think our men do a good job of looking in the mirror, and we got a short week," McCarthy stated, alluding to Pittsburgh's Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos coming up.

    In a recent development, "But yeah, no, we'll sit down and address everything, especially, you know, we need him. We need him in those games, and that's not acceptable to be thrown out of a game. He's one of the 48 [active players]. It's about everything we do through the week is to put those guys in position to be successful.".

    Recent findings suggest that metcalf's first penalty arrived with just under 13 minutes to go in the third quarter. He was blocking DeJean on a 5-yard carry from Pittsburgh running back Jaylen Warren. That turned into extracurricular activity.

    Metcalf and DeJean were tangled up after the play. They had to be separated, and Metcalf was assessed an unnecessary roughness penalty.

    That infraction effectively erased a positive first-down gain by Warren, keeping the Steelers at the doorstep of their own end zone.

    They ended up punting three plays later.

    Recent findings suggest that metcalf clocked out with one catch for two receiving yards in the defeat. He came into the day with 35 receptions, 432 receiving yards and two touchdowns. In the past four games, he's reeled in a combined six passes.

    It has been revealed that in March 2025, the Steelers acquired Metcalf from the Seattle Seahawks in a trade. Pittsburgh gave up a 2025 second-round pick and signed the two-time Pro Bowl receiver to a five-year extension reportedly worth $150 million.

    The Steelers went on to trade wideout George Pickens to the Dallas Cowboys later that offseason.

    Metcalf, a 2019 second-round pick, has been ejected three times since entering the NFL and is tied with San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw for the most disqualifications in that span, according to ESPN. Infamously, Metcalf's aforementioned sideline altercation with a Lions fan last season didn't result in a penalty or an ejection, as it wasn't seen by officials in real time.

    #119367. Retirees face a looming deadline for required withdrawals — missing it could trigger a tax penalty

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (649 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Retirees face a looming deadline for required withdrawals — missing it could trigger a tax penalty

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (649 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that every year, millions of Americans must take required withdrawals from retirement accounts by Dec.
    • Amid the busy holiday season, it's easy to miss the year-end deadline for required minimum distributions — a mistake that can trigger a hefty IRS penalty, experts stated.
    • "One of the most common RMD mistakes is waiting until the last minute," noted certified financial planner Alex Canellopoulos, director of wealth at Vista Capital Partners in Portland, Oregon.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that every year, millions of Americans must take required withdrawals from retirement accounts by Dec. 31.

    Amid the busy holiday season, it's easy to miss the year-end deadline for required minimum distributions — a mistake that can trigger a hefty IRS penalty, experts stated.

    "One of the most common RMD mistakes is waiting until the last minute," noted certified financial planner Alex Canellopoulos, director of wealth at Vista Capital Partners in Portland, Oregon.

    Sources indicate that most retirees must start RMDs from pretax accounts at age 73. The withdrawal is based on the previous year's account balances on Dec. 31, your age and an IRS "life expectancy factor.".

    Sources indicate that the first annual RMD deadline is April 1 of the year after you turn 73, and future withdrawals are due by Dec. 31. If you wait until April 1 for the first one, you'll need two RMDs that year.

    RMDs also apply to certain inherited IRAs if the original IRA owner reached RMD age before their death.

    In 2023, more than 14.8 million taxpayers age 70 or older had a traditional individual retirement account, according to the latest IRS data. The average year-end market value of the accounts was about $330,000.

    Deferring RMDs until the last minute raises the likelihood of mistakes, such as overlooking certain retirement accounts or making withdrawal calculation errors, Canellopoulos stated.

    Some 7% of Vanguard investors at RMD age missed their yearly withdrawal in 2025, up slightly from 6.7% in 2024, according to a Vanguard analysis of about 400,000 RMD-age retirees with IRA balances published in December 2025.

    Among those investors, the average missed RMD was $10,500 in 2025, Vanguard told CNBC.

    Industry observers note that investors who don't take RMDs by the annual deadline may owe an excise tax to the IRS, worth up to 25% of the amount they should have withdrawn. For example, the excise tax could be up to $2,625 for a $10,500 missed RMD.

    If investors miss a required withdrawal, they could reduce the penalty to 10% if they "timely corrected" the RMD within two years and file Form 5329, according to the IRS.

    It has been revealed that in some cases, the IRS could waive the penalty entirely due to "reasonable error" if investors take "reasonable steps" to fix the shortfall, according to the agency. Investors can file Form 5329 with a letter of explanation to request the waiver.

    Industry observers note that "If you don't ask, you're not going to get it," stated certified public accountant Tim Steffen, director of advanced planning at financial services firm Baird. "I've never heard of anybody being denied the waiver.".

    Investors who give to charity may be skipping a specific donation strategy that can reduce or eliminate their annual RMDs, according to Lawrence Pon, a CFP and CPA based in Redwood City, California.

    They can use a so-called qualified charitable distribution, or QCD, Pon mentioned.

    A QCD has a dual tax benefit: It doesn't count as taxable income and may also satisfy at least part of an investor's yearly RMD, Pon said.

    The move requires a direct transfer from an investor's pretax IRA to an eligible nonprofit organization. They can donate up to $111,000 in 2026. While QCD eligibility begins at age 70½, transfers won't start counting toward RMDs until an investor reaches their RMD age.

    Generally, taxpayers only get a tax break for large charitable donations if they itemize deductions on their tax returns. But QCDs still provide a tax benefit for charitable gifts when investors use the standard deduction.

    QCDs "provide a real benefit if you are not itemizing [tax deductions]," noted Pon.

    In a recent development, while there's no tax deduction for QCDs, the transfer won't increase a taxpayer's adjusted gross income, or AGI. Raising AGI can cause other tax consequences, such as higher premiums for Medicare Part B and Part D.

    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Tokenization platform Securitize gains 10% postmarket on Q3 results, move into asset-backed finance

    📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (448 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.
    • Industry observers note that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively newly introduced corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
    • The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    Industry observers note that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively newly introduced corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    Sources indicate that securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    Sources indicate that securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The company posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    According to recent reports, also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and declared the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo noted.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    Breaking: Nvidia stock plunges 14%, wraps up longest weekly losing streak since 2008 financial crisis

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (484 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The last time Wall Street was this down on Nvidia the chipmaker's flagship product was the GeForce graphics processor for high-end PC video games, and markets were reeling from the global financial crisis.
    • Nvidia shares tumbled 14% on Friday, sliding for a seventh straight day as investors grew increasingly concerned about life after co-founder Jensen Huang.
    • In a recent development, shares of Nvidia are down 46% over the period, pushing the organization's market cap down by about $2.6 trillion.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The last time Wall Street was this down on Nvidia the chipmaker's flagship product was the GeForce graphics processor for high-end PC video games, and markets were reeling from the global financial crisis.

    Nvidia shares tumbled 14% on Friday, sliding for a seventh straight day as investors grew increasingly concerned about life after co-founder Jensen Huang. The stock closed lower for a seventh consecutive week, the longest such stretch since 2008.

    In a recent development, shares of Nvidia are down 46% over the period, pushing the organization's market cap down by about $2.6 trillion. The stock is now trading at roughly 8.4 times forward earnings, while Advanced Micro Devices is valued at 29 times profit for the next 12 months.

    On Friday, Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is exploring potential accounting concerns at Nvidia, pushing the stock down further.

    Once the most valuable company in the world, Nvidia now has a market cap of $3 trillion, putting it fourth behind Apple, Microsoft and Alphabet.

    In a recent development, nvidia is reeling from the removal of Huang, who resigned on Nov. 12, after multiple reported affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman who was allegedly a spy.

    Harvey Jones, Nvidia's newly appointed board chair, remarked earlier this week that Huang had resigned after "disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms.".

    But the chipmaker's losing streak started before Nvidia was thrown into crisis as investors worried over the sustainability of the AI buildout, particularly after the midterm elections, and emerging competition in AI chips from Google and AMD.

    In a recent development, even a better-than-expected earnings report, which included an increase to fiscal 2028 guidance, didn't stem the selling. Interim CEO Colette Kress, the company's longtime CFO, projected revenue growth next fiscal year of 75%, and mentioned that customers aren't going anywhere.

    On Tuesday's earnings call with analysts, Kress signed off by saying, "we've got this." In a manufacturer meeting the next day, executives told staff that it was moving its yearly review process, which can come with more stock, from March to December.

    For investors, one major question is whether Nvidia can continue to innovate and sustain its commanding lead in the AI chip market without its visionary leader. Almost the entire organization now is built around the AI trade, a phenomenon that began taking hold just four years ago with the launch of OpenAI's ChatGPT.

    Before that, Nvidia's primary business was selling graphics cards used for video games. In mid-2008, the last time the stock was this deep into a weekly losing streak, Nvidia was generating less than $1 billion per quarter. Now it pulls in more than $1 billion per day. At the time, the entire market was in freefall due to the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

    #119345. What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (752 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (752 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the tech giant's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
    • Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the firm.
    • Recent findings suggest that nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the tech giant's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

    Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the firm. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

    "Although we expect the company to fulfill all of its previously confirmed commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate new multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said in a note Thursday.

    The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

    Recent findings suggest that tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

    On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    Tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

    According to recent reports, it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The firm had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

    In a recent development, neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

    In a recent development, coreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

    It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, stated CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

    "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he stated.

    "However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

    CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

    "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my company every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he remarked in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

    It has been revealed that bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any big changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

    The real matter is just how much money the company will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

    Recent findings suggest that "Big companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he noted. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

    — CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.
